column1: # The generic word each MIPS decode rule carries.
# One row per case label of an instrumented dispatch switch in
# into the per-site tables the decoder consults, and REFUSES in both
# directions: a label with no row here does not generate, and a row that
# names no label of any instrumented switch does not generate either.
# Column 1 is the case label, exactly as translate.c spells it.  Column 2
# is a word from include/exec/insn-dataflow-words.h, or "-" for a rule
# with nothing generic to say, whose reason is then column 3.
# NOR's distinguishing operation is the complement, not the disjunction.
# gen_logic()'s OPC_NOR arm emits tcg_gen_nor_tl when both sources are
# live and tcg_gen_not_tl when either is $zero -- which is the `not
# rd,rs' idiom the assembler spells for rs == $zero -- so every arm of
# the rule complements and only one of them also disjoins.  Wording it
# `or' loses the complement entirely: `not $t2,$t3' published as OR
# reconstructs to the operand instead of to its complement.
